result.title: Honeypots for AI Agent Insider Threats
result.summary: AI agents deployed inside organizations can pose an insider threat if they make mistakes, are compromised by an attacker, or pursue misaligned objectives. We propose honeypots as an AI control method to improve the security of internal agent deployments. Rather than only using honeypots for pre-deployment evaluations, defenders should plant decoy opportunities for harmful actions throughout the production environment to detect misbehavior, incriminate malicious agents, and deter attacks. Such honeypots can elicit misbehavior under real deployment conditions, identify malicious agents even if chain-of-thought monitorability degrades, provide reliable warnings about agent misbehavior to security teams, and scale cheaply to many agent instances. The presence of honeypots also introduces uncertainty about which opportunities are real, thus deterring malicious agents from attacking and reducing the rate of misbehavior. We discuss the limitations of honeypots and give reasons to expect them to remain effective as agent capabilities increase. Finally, we outline key research questions to measure and improve the effectiveness of honeypots: testing the robustness of honeypots, comparing their detection effectiveness with other monitoring methods, understanding their incrimination and deterrence effects, and building supporting infrastructure.

AI.brief_summary: 论文主张把「蜜罐」作为 AI 控制手段：在组织生产环境中布置诱饵机会，以诱发、识别和归责内部代理的有害行为，并讨论其局限、随能力提升仍有效的理由以及待研究问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「主动布置诱饵以触发并检验监控能否发现隐藏行为」的思路，可能可供核查用于设计 LVR 诊断，验证推理是否真正依赖视觉证据、以及内部状态监控的可靠性；但材料本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
